1.mohsin_khan: Ta-Ha. [These letters are one of the miracles of the Quran, and none but Allah (Alone) knows their meanings.]

2.sahih_international: We have not sent down to you the Qur'an that you be distressed
2.pickthall: We have not revealed unto thee (Muhammad) this Qur'an that thou shouldst be distressed,
2.yusuf_ali: We have not sent down the Qur'an to thee to be (an occasion) for thy distress,
2.shakir: We have not revealed the Quran to you that you may be unsuccessful.
2.muhammad_sarwar: We have sent the Quran only as reminder
2.mohsin_khan: We have not sent down the Quran unto you (O Muhammad SAW) to cause you distress,
2.arberry: We have not sent down the Koran upon thee for thee to be unprosperous,

3.sahih_international: But only as a reminder for those who fear [Allah] -
3.pickthall: But as a reminder unto him who feareth,
3.yusuf_ali: But only as an admonition to those who fear (Allah),-
3.shakir: Nay, it is a reminder to him who fears:
3.muhammad_sarwar: for those who have fear (of disobeying God), not to make you, (Muhammad), miserable.
3.mohsin_khan: But only as a Reminder to those who fear (Allah).
3.arberry: but only as a reminder to him who tears,

4.sahih_international: A revelation from He who created the earth and highest heavens,
4.pickthall: A revelation from Him Who created the earth and the high heavens,
4.yusuf_ali: A revelation from Him Who created the earth and the heavens on high.
4.shakir: A revelation from Him Who created the earth and the high heavens.
4.muhammad_sarwar: It is a revelation from the Creator of the earth and the high heavens.
4.mohsin_khan: A revelation from Him (Allah) Who has created the earth and high heavens.
4.arberry: a revelation from Him who created the earth and the high heavens;

5.sahih_international: The Most Merciful [who is] above the Throne established.
5.pickthall: The Beneficent One, Who is established on the Throne.
5.yusuf_ali: (Allah) Most Gracious is firmly established on the throne (of authority).
5.shakir: The Beneficent Allah is firm in power.
5.muhammad_sarwar: The Beneficent God is dominant over the Throne (of the realm).
5.mohsin_khan: The Most Beneficent (Allah) Istawa (rose over) the (Mighty) Throne (in a manner that suits His Majesty).
5.arberry: the All-compassionate sat Himself upon the Throne; to Him belongs

6.sahih_international: To Him belongs what is in the heavens and what is on the earth and what is between them and what is under the soil.
6.pickthall: Unto Him belongeth whatsoever is in the heavens and whatsoever is in the earth, and whatsoever is between them, and whatsoever is beneath the sod.
6.yusuf_ali: To Him belongs what is in the heavens and on earth, and all between them, and all beneath the soil.
6.shakir: His is what is in the heavens and what is in the earth and what is between them two and what is beneath the ground.
6.muhammad_sarwar: To Him belongs all that is in the heavens and the earth, all that lies between them, and lies below the earth.
6.mohsin_khan: To Him belongs all that is in the heavens and all that is on the earth, and all that is between them, and all that is under the soil.
6.arberry: all that is in the heavens and the earth and all that is between them, and all that is underneath the soil.

7.sahih_international: And if you speak aloud - then indeed, He knows the secret and what is [even] more hidden.
7.pickthall: And if thou speakest aloud, then lo! He knoweth the secret (thought) and (that which is yet) more hidden.
7.yusuf_ali: If thou pronounce the word aloud, (it is no matter): for verily He knoweth what is secret and what is yet more hidden.
7.shakir: And if you utter the saying aloud, then surely He knows the secret, and what is yet more hidden.
7.muhammad_sarwar: Whether or not you express (your thoughts) in words, God certainly knows all unspoken thoughts and all that is even more difficult to find.
7.mohsin_khan: And if you (O Muhammad SAW) speak (the invocation) aloud, then verily, He knows the secret and that which is yet more hidden.
7.arberry: Be thou loud in thy speech, yet surely He knows the secret and that yet more hidden.

8.sahih_international: Allah - there is no deity except Him. To Him belong the best names.
8.pickthall: Allah! There is no Allah save Him. His are the most beautiful names.
8.yusuf_ali: Allah! there is no god but He! To Him belong the most Beautiful Names.
8.shakir: Allah-- there is no god but He; His are the very best names.
8.muhammad_sarwar: God is the only Lord and to Him belong all the exalted Names.
8.mohsin_khan: Allah! La ilahla illa Huwa (none has the right to be worshipped but He)! To Him belong the Best Names.
8.arberry: God -- there is no god but He. To Him belong the Names Most Beautiful.

9.sahih_international: And has the story of Moses reached you? -
9.pickthall: Hath there come unto thee the story of Moses?
9.yusuf_ali: Has the story of Moses reached thee?
9.shakir: And has the story of Musa come to you?
9.muhammad_sarwar: (Muhammad), have you heard the story of Moses?
9.mohsin_khan: And has there come to you the story of Musa (Moses)?
9.arberry: Hast thou received the story of Moses?

10.sahih_international: When he saw a fire and said to his family, "Stay here; indeed, I have perceived a fire; perhaps I can bring you a torch or find at the fire some guidance."
10.pickthall: When he saw a fire and said unto his folk: Lo! Wait! I see a fire afar off. Peradventure I may bring you a brand therefrom or may find guidance at the fire.
10.yusuf_ali: Behold, he saw a fire: So he said to his family, "Tarry ye; I perceive a fire; perhaps I can bring you some burning brand therefrom, or find some guidance at the fire."
10.shakir: When he saw fire, he said to his family: Stop, for surely I see a fire, haply I may bring to you therefrom a live coal or find a guidance at the fire.
10.muhammad_sarwar: When he saw the fire, he said to his family, "Wait here for I can see a fire. Perhaps I shall bring you a burning torch or find a way to some fire".
10.mohsin_khan: When he saw a fire, he said to his family: "Wait! Verily, I have seen a fire, perhaps I can bring you some burning brand therefrom, or find some guidance at the fire."
10.arberry: When he saw a fire, and said to his family, 'Tarry you here; I observe a fire. Perhaps I shall bring you a brand from it, or I shall find at the fire guidance.'

11.sahih_international: And when he came to it, he was called, "O Moses,
11.pickthall: And when he reached it, he was called by name: O Moses!
11.yusuf_ali: But when he came to the fire, a voice was heard: "O Moses!
11.shakir: So when he came to it, a voice was uttered: O Musa:
11.muhammad_sarwar: When he came near the fire he was called, "Moses,
11.mohsin_khan: And when he came to it (the fire), he was called by name: "O Musa (Moses)!
11.arberry: When he came to it, a voice cried, 'Moses,

12.sahih_international: Indeed, I am your Lord, so remove your sandals. Indeed, you are in the sacred valley of Tuwa.
12.pickthall: Lo! I, even I, am thy Lord, So take off thy shoes, for lo! thou art in the holy valley of Tuwa.
12.yusuf_ali: "Verily I am thy Lord! therefore (in My presence) put off thy shoes: thou art in the sacred valley Tuwa.
12.shakir: Surely I am your Lord, therefore put off your shoes; surely you are in the sacred valley, Tuwa,
12.muhammad_sarwar: I Am your Lord. Take off your shoes; you are in the holy valley of Tuwa.
12.mohsin_khan: "Verily! I am your Lord! So take off your shoes, you are in the sacred valley, Tuwa.
12.arberry: I am thy Lord; put off thy shoes; thou art in the holy valley, Towa.

13.sahih_international: And I have chosen you, so listen to what is revealed [to you].
13.pickthall: And I have chosen thee, so hearken unto that which is inspired.
13.yusuf_ali: "I have chosen thee: listen, then, to the inspiration (sent to thee).
13.shakir: And I have chosen you, so listen to what is revealed:
13.muhammad_sarwar: I have chosen you as My Messengers. Listen to the revelation.
13.mohsin_khan: "And I have chosen you. So listen to that which is inspired to you.
13.arberry: I Myself have chosen thee; therefore give thou ear to this revelation.

14.sahih_international: Indeed, I am Allah. There is no deity except Me, so worship Me and establish prayer for My remembrance.
14.pickthall: Lo! I, even I, am Allah, There is no Allah save Me. So serve Me and establish worship for My remembrance.
14.yusuf_ali: "Verily, I am Allah: There is no god but I: So serve thou Me (only), and establish regular prayer for celebrating My praise.
14.shakir: Surely I am Allah, there is no god but I, therefore serve Me and keep up prayer for My remembrance:
14.muhammad_sarwar: I Am the only God. Worship Me and be steadfast in prayer to have My name always in your mind.
14.mohsin_khan: "Verily! I am Allah! La ilaha illa Ana (none has the right to be worshipped but I), so worship Me, and perform As-Salat (Iqamat-as-Salat) for My Remembrance.
14.arberry: Verily I am God; there is no god but I; therefore serve Me, and perform the prayer of My remembrance.

15.sahih_international: Indeed, the Hour is coming - I almost conceal it - so that every soul may be recompensed according to that for which it strives.
15.pickthall: Lo! the Hour is surely coming. But I will to keep it hidden, that every soul may be rewarded for that which it striveth (to achieve).
15.yusuf_ali: "Verily the Hour is coming - My design is to keep it hidden - for every soul to receive its reward by the measure of its Endeavour.
15.shakir: Surely the hour is coming-- I am about to make it manifest-- so that every soul may be rewarded as it strives:
15.muhammad_sarwar: Although it is certain that the Day of Judgment will come, I prefer to keep it almost a secret so that every soul will receive the recompense for what it has done (on its own).
15.mohsin_khan: "Verily, the Hour is coming and My Will is to keep it hidden that every person may be rewarded for that which he strives.
15.arberry: The Hour is coming; I would conceal it that every soul may be recompensed for its labours.

16.sahih_international: So do not let one avert you from it who does not believe in it and follows his desire, for you [then] would perish.
16.pickthall: Therefor, let not him turn thee aside from (the thought of) it who believeth not therein but followeth his own desire, lest thou perish.
16.yusuf_ali: "Therefore let not such as believe not therein but follow their own lusts, divert thee therefrom, lest thou perish!"..
16.shakir: Therefore let not him who believes not in it and follows his low desires turn you away from it so that you should perish;
16.muhammad_sarwar: Let not the unbelievers who follow their vain desires make you forget the Day of Judgment, lest you will perish."
16.mohsin_khan: "Therefore, let not the one who believes not therein (i.e. in the Day of Resurrection, Reckoning, Paradise and Hell, etc.), but follows his own lusts, divert you therefrom, lest you perish.
16.arberry: Let none bar thee from it, that believes not in it but follows after his own caprice, or thou wilt perish.

17.sahih_international: And what is that in your right hand, O Moses?"
17.pickthall: And what is that in thy right hand, O Moses?
17.yusuf_ali: "And what is that in the right hand, O Moses?"
17.shakir: And what is this in your right hand, O Musa!
17.muhammad_sarwar: The Lord asked, "Moses, what is in your right hand?"
17.mohsin_khan: "And what is that in your right hand, O Musa (Moses)?"
17.arberry: What is that, Moses, thou hast in thy right hand?'

18.sahih_international: He said, "It is my staff; I lean upon it, and I bring down leaves for my sheep and I have therein other uses."
18.pickthall: He said: This is my staff whereon I lean, and wherewith I bear down branches for my sheep, and wherein I find other uses.
18.yusuf_ali: He said, "It is my rod: on it I lean; with it I beat down fodder for my flocks; and in it I find other uses."
18.shakir: He said: This is my staff: I recline on it and I beat the leaves with it to make them fall upon my sheep, and I have other uses for it.
18.muhammad_sarwar: He replied, "It is my staff. I lean on it, bring down leaves for my sheep with it and I need it for other reasons.
18.mohsin_khan: He said: "This is my stick, whereon I lean, and wherewith I beat down branches for my sheep, and wherein I find other uses."
18.arberry: 'Why, it is my staff,' said Moses. 'I lean upon it, and with it I beat down leaves to feed my sheep; other uses also I find in it.

19.pickthall: He said: Cast it down, O Moses!
19.shakir: He said: Cast it down, O Musa!
19.muhammad_sarwar: The Lord said, "Moses, throw it on the ground".

20.sahih_international: So he threw it down, and thereupon it was a snake, moving swiftly.
20.pickthall: So he cast it down, and lo! it was a serpent, gliding.
20.yusuf_ali: He threw it, and behold! It was a snake, active in motion.
20.shakir: So he cast it down; and lo! it was a serpent running.
20.muhammad_sarwar: Moses threw it on the ground and suddenly he saw that it was a moving serpent.
20.mohsin_khan: He cast it down, and behold! It was a snake, moving quickly.
20.arberry: and he cast it down, and behold it was a serpent sliding.

21.sahih_international: [Allah] said, "Seize it and fear not; We will return it to its former condition.
21.pickthall: He said: Grasp it and fear not. We shall return it to its former state.
21.yusuf_ali: (Allah) said, "Seize it, and fear not: We shall return it at once to its former condition"..
21.shakir: He said: Take hold of it and fear not; We will restore it to its former state:
21.muhammad_sarwar: The Lord said, "Hold the serpent and do not be afraid; We will bring it back to its original form."
21.mohsin_khan: Allah said:"Grasp it, and fear not, We shall return it to its former state,
21.arberry: Said He, 'Take it, and fear not; We will restore it to its first state.

22.sahih_international: And draw in your hand to your side; it will come out white without disease - another sign,
22.pickthall: And thrust thy hand within thine armpit, it will come forth white without hurt. (That will be) another token.
22.yusuf_ali: "Now draw thy hand close to thy side: It shall come forth white (and shining), without harm (or stain),- as another Sign,-
22.shakir: And press your hand to your side, it shall come out white without evil: another sign:
22.muhammad_sarwar: "Now - as another Sign - place your hand under your arm and it will come out sheer white without harm (or stain).
22.mohsin_khan: "And press your (right) hand to your (left) side, it will come forth white (and shining), without any disease as another sign,
22.arberry: Now clasp thy hand to thy arm-pit; it shall come forth white, without evil. That is a second sign.

23.sahih_international: That We may show you [some] of Our greater signs.
23.pickthall: That We may show thee (some) of Our greater portents,
23.yusuf_ali: "In order that We may show thee (two) of our Greater Signs.
23.shakir: That We may show you of Our greater signs:
23.muhammad_sarwar: This We have done to show you some of Our greater miracles.
23.mohsin_khan: "That We may show you (some) of Our Greater Signs.
23.arberry: So We would show thee some of Our greatest signs.

24.sahih_international: Go to Pharaoh. Indeed, he has transgressed."
24.pickthall: Go thou unto Pharaoh! Lo! he hath transgressed (the bounds).
24.yusuf_ali: "Go thou to Pharaoh, for he has indeed transgressed all bounds."
24.shakir: Go to Firon, surely he has exceeded all limits.
24.muhammad_sarwar: Go to the Pharaoh; he has become a rebel."
24.mohsin_khan: "Go to Fir'aun (Pharaoh)! Verily, he has transgressed (all bounds in disbelief and disobedience, and has behaved as an arrogant, and as a tyrant)."
24.arberry: Go to Pharaoh; he has waxed insolent.'

25.sahih_international: [Moses] said, "My Lord, expand for me my breast [with assurance]
25.pickthall: (Moses) said: My Lord! relieve my mind
25.yusuf_ali: (Moses) said: "O my Lord! expand me my breast;
25.shakir: He said: O my Lord! Expand my breast for me,
25.mohsin_khan: [Musa (Moses)] said: "O my Lord! Open for me my chest (grant me self-confidence, contentment, and boldness).

26.sahih_international: And ease for me my task
26.pickthall: And ease my task for me;
26.shakir: And make my affair easy to me,
26.arberry: 'and do Thou ease for me my task.

27.sahih_international: And untie the knot from my tongue
27.pickthall: And loose a knot from my tongue,
27.yusuf_ali: "And remove the impediment from my speech,
27.shakir: And loose the knot from my tongue,
27.mohsin_khan: "And make loose the knot (the defect) from my tongue, (i.e. remove the incorrectness from my speech) [That occurred as a result of a brand of fire which Musa (Moses) put in his mouth when he was an infant]. [Tafsir At-Tabari, Vol. 16, Page 159].
27.arberry: Unloose the knot upon my tongue, t

28.sahih_international: That they may understand my speech.
28.pickthall: That they may understand my saying.
28.yusuf_ali: "So they may understand what I say:
28.muhammad_sarwar: so that they may understand me.
28.arberry: hat they may understand my words.

29.sahih_international: And appoint for me a minister from my family -
29.pickthall: Appoint for me a henchman from my folk,
29.yusuf_ali: "And give me a Minister from my family,
29.shakir: And give to me an aider from my family:
29.muhammad_sarwar: Appoint a deputy (for me) from my own people.
29.mohsin_khan: "And appoint for me a helper from my family,
29.arberry: Appoint for me of my folk a familiar,

30.muhammad_sarwar: Let it be my brother Aaron

32.sahih_international: And let him share my task
32.pickthall: And let him share my task,
32.shakir: And associate him (with me) in my affair,
32.muhammad_sarwar: Let him be my partner in this task
32.mohsin_khan: "And let him share my task (of conveying Allah's Message and Prophethood),
32.arberry: and associate him with me in my task.

33.sahih_international: That we may exalt You much
33.pickthall: That we may glorify Thee much
33.yusuf_ali: "That we may celebrate Thy praise without stint,
33.shakir: So that we should glorify Thee much,

35.sahih_international: Indeed, You are of us ever Seeing."
35.pickthall: Lo! Thou art ever Seeing us.
35.yusuf_ali: "For Thou art He that (ever) regardeth us."
35.muhammad_sarwar: You are Well Aware of our situation."
35.mohsin_khan: "Verily! You are of us Ever a Well-Seer."

36.sahih_international: [Allah] said, "You have been granted your request, O Moses.
36.pickthall: He said: Thou art granted thy request, O Moses.
36.yusuf_ali: (Allah) said: "Granted is thy prayer, O Moses!"
36.shakir: He said: You are indeed granted your petition, O Musa
36.muhammad_sarwar: The Lord said, "Moses, your request is granted.
36.mohsin_khan: Allah said: "You are granted your request, O Musa (Moses)!
36.arberry: Said He, 'Thou art granted, Moses, thy petition.

37.sahih_international: And We had already conferred favor upon you another time,
37.pickthall: And indeed, another time, already We have shown thee favour,
37.yusuf_ali: "And indeed We conferred a favour on thee another time (before).
37.shakir: And certainly We bestowed on you a favor at another time;
37.muhammad_sarwar: It is the second time that We have bestowed upon you Our favor.
37.mohsin_khan: "And indeed We conferred a favour on you another time (before).
37.arberry: Already another time We favoured thee,

38.sahih_international: When We inspired to your mother what We inspired,
38.pickthall: When we inspired in thy mother that which is inspired,
38.yusuf_ali: "Behold! We sent to thy mother, by inspiration, the message:
38.shakir: When We revealed to your mother what was revealed;
38.muhammad_sarwar: Remember when We inspired your mother with a certain inspiration
38.mohsin_khan: "When We inspired your mother with that which We inspired.
38.arberry: when We revealed what was revealed unto thy mother:

39.sahih_international: [Saying], 'Cast him into the chest and cast it into the river, and the river will throw it onto the bank; there will take him an enemy to Me and an enemy to him.' And I bestowed upon you love from Me that you would be brought up under My eye.
39.pickthall: Saying: Throw him into the ark, and throw it into the river, then the river shall throw it on to the bank, and there an enemy to Me and an enemy to him shall take him. And I endued thee with love from Me that thou mightest be trained according to My will,
39.yusuf_ali: "'Throw (the child) into the chest, and throw (the chest) into the river: the river will cast him up on the bank, and he will be taken up by one who is an enemy to Me and an enemy to him': But I cast (the garment of) love over thee from Me: and (this) in order that thou mayest be reared under Mine eye.
39.shakir: Saying: Put him into a chest, then cast it down into the river, then the river shall throw him on the shore; there shall take him up one who is an enemy to Me and enemy to him, and I cast down upon you love from Me, and that you might be brought up before My eyes;
39.muhammad_sarwar: to lace her child in a chest and throw it into the sea which would hurl it towards the shore. Then an enemy of Mine who was also the enemy of the child would pick it up from there. I made you attractive and loveable so that you would be reared before My own eyes.
39.mohsin_khan: "Saying: 'Put him (the child) into the Tabut (a box or a case or a chest) and put it into the river (Nile), then the river shall cast it up on the bank, and there, an enemy of Mine and an enemy of his shall take him.' And I endued you with love from Me, in order that you may be brought up under My Eye,
39.arberry: "Cast him into the ark, and cast him into the river, and let the river throw him up on the shore. An enemy of Mine and his shall take him." And I loaded on thee love from Me, and to be formed in My sight,

40.sahih_international: [And We favored you] when your sister went and said, 'Shall I direct you to someone who will be responsible for him?' So We restored you to your mother that she might be content and not grieve. And you killed someone, but We saved you from retaliation and tried you with a [severe] trial. And you remained [some] years among the people of Madyan. Then you came [here] at the decreed time, O Moses.
40.pickthall: When thy sister went and said: Shall I show you one who will nurse him? and we restored thee to thy mother that her eyes might be refreshed and might not sorrow. And thou didst kill a man and We delivered thee from great distress, and tried thee with a heavy trial. And thou didst tarry years among the folk of Midian. Then camest thou (hither) by (My) providence, O Moses,
40.yusuf_ali: "Behold! thy sister goeth forth and saith, 'shall I show you one who will nurse and rear the (child)?' So We brought thee back to thy mother, that her eye might be cooled and she should not grieve. Then thou didst slay a man, but We saved thee from trouble, and We tried thee in various ways. Then didst thou tarry a number of years with the people of Midian. Then didst thou come hither as ordained, O Moses!
40.shakir: When your sister went and said: Shall I direct you to one who will take charge of him? So We brought you back to your mother, that her eye might be cooled and she should not grieve and you killed a man, then We delivered you from the grief, and We tried you with (a severe) trying. Then you stayed for years among the people of Madyan; then you came hither as ordained, O Musa.
40.muhammad_sarwar: Your sister went to them and said, "May I show you someone who will nurse this child?" We returned you to your mother to make her rejoice and forget her grief. You slew a man and We saved you from trouble. We tried you through various trials. Then you stayed some years with the people of Midian (Shu'ayb and his family) and after that you came back to Egypt as was ordained.
40.mohsin_khan: "When your sister went and said: 'Shall I show you one who will nurse him?' So We restored you to your mother, that she might cool her eyes and she should not grieve. Then you did kill a man, but We saved you from great distress and tried you with a heavy trial. Then you stayed a number of years with the people of Madyan (Midian). Then you came here according to the fixed term which I ordained (for you), O Musa (Moses)!
40.arberry: when thy sister went out, saying, "Shall I point you to one to have charge of him?" So We returned thee to thy mother that she might rejoice, and not sorrow. Then thou slewest; a living soul, and We delivered thee out of grief, and We tried thee with many trials. Many years among the people of Midian thou didst sojourn, then camest hither, Moses, according to a decree.

41.sahih_international: And I produced you for Myself.
41.pickthall: And I have attached thee to Myself.
41.yusuf_ali: "And I have prepared thee for Myself (for service)"..
41.shakir: And I have chosen you for Myself:
41.arberry: I have chosen thee for My service;

42.sahih_international: Go, you and your brother, with My signs and do not slacken in My remembrance.
42.pickthall: Go, thou and thy brother, with My tokens, and be not faint in remembrance of Me.
42.yusuf_ali: "Go, thou and thy brother, with My Signs, and slacken not, either of you, in keeping Me in remembrance.
42.shakir: Go you and your brother with My communications and be not remiss in remembering Me;
42.muhammad_sarwar: "Go with your brother. Take My miracles and do not be reluctant in preaching My message.
42.mohsin_khan: "Go you and your brother with My Ayat (proofs, evidences, verses, lessons, signs, revelations, etc.), and do not, you both, slacken and become weak in My Remembrance.
42.arberry: go therefore, thou and thy brother; with My signs, and neglect not to remember Me.

43.sahih_international: Go, both of you, to Pharaoh. Indeed, he has transgressed.
43.pickthall: Go, both of you, unto Pharaoh. Lo! he hath transgressed (the bounds).
43.yusuf_ali: "Go, both of you, to Pharaoh, for he has indeed transgressed all bounds;
43.shakir: Go both to Firon, surely he has become inordinate;
43.muhammad_sarwar: Go both of you to the Pharaoh; he has become a rebel.
43.mohsin_khan: "Go, both of you, to Fir'aun (Pharaoh), verily, he has transgressed (all bounds in disbelief and disobedience and behaved as an arrogant and as a tyrant).
43.arberry: Go to Pharaoh, for he has waxed insolent;

44.sahih_international: And speak to him with gentle speech that perhaps he may be reminded or fear [Allah]."
44.pickthall: And speak unto him a gentle word, that peradventure he may heed or fear.
44.yusuf_ali: "But speak to him mildly; perchance he may take warning or fear (Allah)."
44.shakir: Then speak to him a gentle word haply he may mind or fear.
44.muhammad_sarwar: Both of you must speak with him in a gentle manner so that perhaps he may come to himself or have fear (of God)."
44.mohsin_khan: "And speak to him mildly, perhaps he may accept admonition or fear Allah."
44.arberry: yet speak gently to him, that haply he may be mindful, or perchance fear.'

45.sahih_international: They said, "Our Lord, indeed we are afraid that he will hasten [punishment] against us or that he will transgress."
45.pickthall: They said: Our Lord! Lo! we fear that he may be beforehand with us or that he may play the tyrant.
45.yusuf_ali: They (Moses and Aaron) said: "Our Lord! We fear lest he hasten with insolence against us, or lest he transgress all bounds."
45.shakir: Both said: O our Lord! Surely we fear that he may hasten to do evil to us or that he may become inordinate.
45.muhammad_sarwar: They said, "Lord, we are afraid of his transgression and rebellion against us".
45.mohsin_khan: They said: "Our Lord! Verily! We fear lest he should hasten to punish us or lest he should transgress (all bounds against us)."
45.arberry: 'O our Lord,' said Moses and Aaron, 'truly we fear he may exceed against us, or wax insolent.'

46.sahih_international: [Allah] said, "Fear not. Indeed, I am with you both; I hear and I see.
46.pickthall: He said: Fear not. Lo! I am with you twain, Hearing and Seeing.
46.yusuf_ali: He said: "Fear not: for I am with you: I hear and see (everything).
46.shakir: He said: Fear not, surely I am with you both: I do hear and see.
46.muhammad_sarwar: The Lord replied them, "Do not be afraid; I Am with you all the time, listening and seeing."
46.mohsin_khan: He (Allah) said: "Fear not, verily! I am with you both, hearing and seeing.
46.arberry: 'Fear not,' said He. 'Surely I shall be with you, hearing and seeing.

47.sahih_international: So go to him and say, 'Indeed, we are messengers of your Lord, so send with us the Children of Israel and do not torment them. We have come to you with a sign from your Lord. And peace will be upon he who follows the guidance.
47.pickthall: So go ye unto him and say: Lo! we are two messengers of thy Lord. So let the children of Israel go with us, and torment them not. We bring thee a token from thy Lord. And peace will be for him who followeth right guidance.
47.yusuf_ali: "So go ye both to him, and say, 'Verily we are messengers sent by thy Lord: Send forth, therefore, the Children of Israel with us, and afflict them not: with a Sign, indeed, have we come from thy Lord! and peace to all who follow guidance!
47.shakir: So go you both to him and say: Surely we are two apostles of your Lord; therefore send the children of Israel with us and do not torment them! Indeed we have brought to you a communication from your Lord, and peace is on him who follows the guidance;
47.muhammad_sarwar: They came to the Pharaoh and told him that they were the Messengerss of his Lord and that they wanted him to let the Israelites go with them and stop afflicting the Israelites with torment. They told the Pharaoh, "We have brought miracles from Our Creator. Peace be with those who follow the right guidance.
47.mohsin_khan: "So go you both to him, and say: 'Verily, we are Messengers of your Lord, so let the Children of Israel go with us, and torment them not; indeed, we have come with a sign from your Lord! And peace will be upon him who follows the guidance!
47.arberry: So go you both to Pharaoh, and say, "We are the Messengers of thy Lord, so send forth with us the Children of Israel and chastise them not; we have brought thee a sign from thy Lord; and peace be upon him who follows the guidance!

48.sahih_international: Indeed, it has been revealed to us that the punishment will be upon whoever denies and turns away.' "
48.pickthall: Lo! it hath been revealed unto us that the doom will be for him who denieth and turneth away.
48.yusuf_ali: "'Verily it has been revealed to us that the Penalty (awaits) those who reject and turn away.'"
48.shakir: Surely it has been revealed to us that the chastisement will surely come upon him who rejects and turns back.
48.muhammad_sarwar: It is revealed to us that those who call our message a lie or turn away from it will face the torment."
48.mohsin_khan: 'Truly, it has been revealed to us that the torment will be for him who denies [believes not in the Oneness of Allah, and in His Messengers, etc.], and turns away.'(from the truth and obedience of Allah)"
48.arberry: It has been revealed to us that chastisement shall light upon him who cries lies and turns his back."

49.sahih_international: [Pharaoh] said, "So who is the Lord of you two, O Moses?"
49.pickthall: (Pharaoh) said: Who then is the Lord of you twain, O Moses?
49.yusuf_ali: (When this message was delivered), (Pharaoh) said: "Who, then, O Moses, is the Lord of you two?"
49.shakir: (Firon) said: And who is your Lord, O Musa?
49.muhammad_sarwar: The Pharaoh asked them, "Who is your Lord?"
49.mohsin_khan: Fir'aun (Pharaoh) said: "Who then, O Musa (Moses), is the Lord of you two?"
49.arberry: Pharaoh said, 'Who is your Lord, Moses?'

50.sahih_international: He said, "Our Lord is He who gave each thing its form and then guided [it]."
50.pickthall: He said: Our Lord is He Who gave unto everything its nature, then guided it aright.
50.yusuf_ali: He said: "Our Lord is He Who gave to each (created) thing its form and nature, and further, gave (it) guidance."
50.shakir: He said: Our Lord is He Who gave to everything its creation, then guided it (to its goal).
50.muhammad_sarwar: They replied, "Our Lord is the One Who has created all things and has given guidance".
50.mohsin_khan: [Musa (Moses)] said: "Our Lord is He Who gave to each thing its form and nature, then guided it aright."
50.arberry: He said, 'Our Lord is He who gave everything its creation, then guided it.'

51.sahih_international: [Pharaoh] said, "Then what is the case of the former generations?"
51.pickthall: He said: What then is the state of the generations of old?
51.yusuf_ali: (Pharaoh) said: "What then is the condition of previous generations?"
51.shakir: He said: Then what is the state of the former generations?
51.muhammad_sarwar: He then asked, "What do you know about the past generations?"
51.mohsin_khan: [Fir'aun (Pharaoh)] said: "What about the generations of old?"
51.arberry: Pharaoh said, 'And what of the former generations?'

52.sahih_international: [Moses] said, "The knowledge thereof is with my Lord in a record. My Lord neither errs nor forgets."
52.pickthall: He said: The knowledge thereof is with my Lord in a Record. My Lord neither erreth nor forgetteth,
52.yusuf_ali: He replied: "The knowledge of that is with my Lord, duly recorded: my Lord never errs, nor forgets,-
52.shakir: He said: The knowledge thereof is with my Lord in a book, my Lord errs not, nor does He forget;
52.muhammad_sarwar: Moses replied, "The knowledge about it is with my Lord in the Book. My Lord is free from error and forgetfulness.
52.mohsin_khan: [Musa (Moses)] said: "The knowledge thereof is with my Lord, in a Record. My Lord is neither unaware nor He forgets, "
52.arberry: Said Moses, 'The knowledge of them is with my Lord, in a Book; my Lord goes not astray, nor forgets --

53.sahih_international: [It is He] who has made for you the earth as a bed [spread out] and inserted therein for you roadways and sent down from the sky, rain and produced thereby categories of various plants.
53.pickthall: Who hath appointed the earth as a bed and hath threaded roads for you therein and hath sent down water from the sky and thereby We have brought forth divers kinds of vegetation,
53.yusuf_ali: "He Who has, made for you the earth like a carpet spread out; has enabled you to go about therein by roads (and channels); and has sent down water from the sky." With it have We produced diverse pairs of plants each separate from the others.
53.shakir: Who made the earth for you an expanse and made for you therein paths and sent down water from the cloud; then thereby We have brought forth many species of various herbs.
53.muhammad_sarwar: It is God who has made the earth as a cradle for you with roads for you to travel. He has sent water from the sky to produce various pairs of plants.
53.mohsin_khan: Who has made earth for you like a bed (spread out); and has opened roads (ways and paths etc.) for you therein; and has sent down water (rain) from the sky. And We have brought forth with it various kinds of vegetation.
53.arberry: He who appointed the earth to be a cradle for you, and therein threaded roads for you, and sent down water out of heaven, and therewith We have brought forth divers kinds of plants.

54.sahih_international: Eat [therefrom] and pasture your livestock. Indeed, in that are signs for those of intelligence.
54.pickthall: (Saying): Eat ye and feed your cattle. Lo! herein verily are portents for men of thought.
54.yusuf_ali: Eat (for yourselves) and pasture your cattle: verily, in this are Signs for men endued with understanding.
54.shakir: Eat and pasture your cattle; most surely there are signs in this for those endowed with understanding.
54.muhammad_sarwar: Consume them as food or for grazing your cattle. In this there is evidence (of the existence of God) for the people of reason".
54.mohsin_khan: Eat and pasture your cattle, (therein); verily, in this are proofs and signs for men of understanding.
54.arberry: Do you eat, and pasture your cattle! Surely in that are signs for men possessing reason.

55.sahih_international: From the earth We created you, and into it We will return you, and from it We will extract you another time.
55.pickthall: Thereof We created you, and thereunto We return you, and thence We bring you forth a second time.
55.yusuf_ali: From the (earth) did We create you, and into it shall We return you, and from it shall We bring you out once again.
55.shakir: From it We created you and into it We shall send you back and from it will We raise you a second time.
55.muhammad_sarwar: We have created you from the earth to which We will return you and will bring you back to life again.
55.mohsin_khan: Thereof (the earth) We created you, and into it We shall return you, and from it We shall bring you out once again.
55.arberry: Out of the earth We created you, and We shall restore you into it, and bring you forth from it a second time.'

56.sahih_international: And We certainly showed Pharaoh Our signs - all of them - but he denied and refused.
56.pickthall: And We verily did show him all Our tokens, but he denied them and refused.
56.yusuf_ali: And We showed Pharaoh all Our Signs, but he did reject and refuse.
56.shakir: And truly We showed him Our signs, all of them, but he rejected and refused.
56.muhammad_sarwar: We showed the Pharaoh all of Our miracles, but he called them lies and turned away from them.
56.mohsin_khan: And indeed We showed him [Fir'aun (Pharaoh)] all Our Signs and Evidences, but he denied and refused.
56.arberry: So We showed Pharaoh all Our signs, but he cried lies, and refused.

57.sahih_international: He said, "Have you come to us to drive us out of our land with your magic, O Moses?
57.pickthall: He said: Hast come to drive us out from our land by thy magic, O Moses?
57.yusuf_ali: He said: "Hast thou come to drive us out of our land with thy magic, O Moses?
57.shakir: Said he: Have you come to us that you should turn us out of our land by your magic, O Musa?
57.muhammad_sarwar: He said to Moses, "Have you come to expel us from our land through your magic?
57.mohsin_khan: He [Fir'aun (Pharaoh)] said: "Have you come to drive us out of our land with your magic, O Musa (Moses)?
57.arberry: 'Hast thou come, Moses,' he said, 'to expel us out of our land

58.sahih_international: Then we will surely bring you magic like it, so make between us and you an appointment, which we will not fail to keep and neither will you, in a place assigned."
58.pickthall: But we surely can produce for thee magic the like thereof; so appoint a tryst between us and you, which neither we nor thou shall fail to keep, at a place convenient (to us both).
58.yusuf_ali: "But we can surely produce magic to match thine! So make a tryst between us and thee, which we shall not fail to keep - neither we nor thou - in a place where both shall have even chances."
58.shakir: So we too will produce before you magic like it, therefore make between us and you an appointment, which we should not break, (neither) we nor you, (in) a central place.
58.muhammad_sarwar: We shall also answer you by magic. Let us make an appointment for a contest among us and let each of us be present at a certain time in the appointed place".
58.mohsin_khan: "Then verily, we can produce magic the like thereof; so appoint a meeting between us and you, which neither we, nor you shall fail to keep, in an open wide place where both shall have a just and equal chance (and beholders could witness the competition)."
58.arberry: by thy sorcery? We shall assuredly bring thee sorcery the like of it; therefore appoint a tryst between us and thee, a place mutually agreeable, and we shall not fail it, neither thou.'

59.sahih_international: [Moses] said, "Your appointment is on the day of the festival when the people assemble at mid-morning."
59.pickthall: (Moses) said: Your tryst shall be the day of the feast, and let the people assemble when the sun hath risen high.
59.yusuf_ali: Moses said: "Your tryst is the Day of the Festival, and let the people be assembled when the sun is well up."
59.shakir: (Musa) said: Your appointment is the day of the Festival and let the people be gathered together in the early forenoon.
59.muhammad_sarwar: Moses said, "Let the contest take place on the Day of Feast so that all the people can come together during the brightness of the day."
59.mohsin_khan: [Musa (Moses)] said: "Your appointed meeting is the day of the festival, and let the people assemble when the sun has risen (forenoon)."
59.arberry: 'Your tryst shall be upon the Feast Day.' said Moses. 'Let the people be mustered at the high noon.'

60.sahih_international: So Pharaoh went away, put together his plan, and then came [to Moses].
60.pickthall: Then Pharaoh went and gathered his strength, then came (to the appointed tryst).
60.yusuf_ali: So Pharaoh withdrew: He concerted his plan, and then came (back).
60.shakir: So Firon turned his back and settled his plan, then came.
60.muhammad_sarwar: The Pharaoh returned to organize his plans and then attended the appointment.
60.mohsin_khan: So Fir'aun (Pharaoh) withdrew, devised his plot and then came back.
60.arberry: Pharaoh then withdrew, and gathered his guile. Thereafter he came again,

61.sahih_international: Moses said to the magicians summoned by Pharaoh, "Woe to you! Do not invent a lie against Allah or He will exterminate you with a punishment; and he has failed who invents [such falsehood]."
61.pickthall: Moses said unto them: Woe unto you! Invent not a lie against Allah, lest He extirpate you by some punishment. He who lieth faileth miserably.
61.yusuf_ali: Moses said to him: Woe to you! Forge not ye a lie against Allah, lest He destroy you (at once) utterly by chastisement: the forger must suffer frustration!"
61.shakir: Musa said to them: Woe to you! do not forge a lie against Allah, lest He destroy you by a punishment, and he who forges (a lie) indeed fails to attain (his desire).
61.muhammad_sarwar: Moses told them, (the magicians) "Woe to you if you invent falsehood against God; you will be destroyed by the torment. Whoever invents falsehood against God will certainly be lost."
61.mohsin_khan: Musa (Moses) said to them: "Woe unto you! Invent not a lie against Allah, lest He should destroy you completely by a torment. And surely, he who invents a lie (against Allah) will fail miserably."
61.arberry: and Moses said to them, 'O beware! Forge not a lie against God, lest He destroy you with a chastisement. Whoso forges has ever failed.'

62.sahih_international: So they disputed over their affair among themselves and concealed their private conversation.
62.pickthall: Then they debated one with another what they must do, and they kept their counsel secret.
62.yusuf_ali: So they disputed, one with another, over their affair, but they kept their talk secret.
62.shakir: So they disputed with one another about their affair and kept the discourse secret.
62.muhammad_sarwar: They started arguing and whispering to each other
62.mohsin_khan: Then they debated with one another what they must do, and they kept their talk secret.
62.arberry: And they disputed upon their plan between them, and communed secretly

63.sahih_international: They said, "Indeed, these are two magicians who want to drive you out of your land with their magic and do away with your most exemplary way.
63.pickthall: They said: Lo! these are two wizards who would drive you out from your country by their magic, and destroy your best traditions;
63.yusuf_ali: They said: "These two are certainly (expert) magicians: their object is to drive you out from your land with their magic, and to do away with your most cherished institutions.
63.shakir: They said: These are most surely two magicians who wish to turn you out from your land by their magic and to take away your best traditions.
63.muhammad_sarwar: and said, "These two people are magicians. They want to expel you from your land through their magic and to destroy your own tradition.
63.mohsin_khan: They said: "Verily! These are two magicians. Their object is to drive you out from your land with magic, and overcome your chiefs and nobles.
63.arberry: saying, 'These two men are sorcerers and their purpose is to expel you out of your land by their sorcery, and to extirpate your justest way.

64.sahih_international: So resolve upon your plan and then come [forward] in line. And he has succeeded today who overcomes."
64.pickthall: So arrange your plan, and come in battle line. Whoso is uppermost this day will be indeed successful.
64.yusuf_ali: "Therefore concert your plan, and then assemble in (serried) ranks: He wins (all along) today who gains the upper hand."
64.shakir: Therefore settle your plan, then come standing in ranks and he will prosper indeed this day who overcomes.
64.muhammad_sarwar: Bring together your devices and come forward in ranks; the winner will, certainly, have great happiness".
64.mohsin_khan: "So devise your plot, and then assemble in line. And whoever overcomes this day will be indeed successful."
64.arberry: So gather your guile; then come in battle-line. Whoever today gains the upper hand shall surely prosper.

65.sahih_international: They said, "O Moses, either you throw or we will be the first to throw."
65.pickthall: They said: O Moses! Either throw first, or let us be the first to throw?
65.yusuf_ali: They said: "O Moses! whether wilt thou that thou throw (first) or that we be the first to throw?"
65.shakir: They said: O Musa! will you cast, or shall we be the first who cast down?
65.muhammad_sarwar: They said, "Moses, would you be the first to show your skill or should we be the first to throw down our devices?"
65.mohsin_khan: They said:"O Musa (Moses)! Either you throw first or we be the first to throw?"
65.arberry: They said, 'Moses, either thou wilt cast, or we shall be the first to cast.'

66.sahih_international: He said, "Rather, you throw." And suddenly their ropes and staffs seemed to him from their magic that they were moving [like snakes].
66.pickthall: He said: Nay, do ye throw! Then lo! their cords and their staves, by their magic, appeared to him as though they ran.
66.yusuf_ali: He said, "Nay, throw ye first!" Then behold their ropes and their rods-so it seemed to him on account of their magic - began to be in lively motion!
66.shakir: He said: Nay! cast down. then lo! their cords and their rods-- it was imaged to him on account of their magic as if they were running.
66.muhammad_sarwar: Moses said, "You throw first." When they did, their ropes and staffs through their magic seemed to be moving.
66.mohsin_khan: [Musa (Moses)] said: "Nay, throw you (first)!" Then behold, their ropes and their sticks, by their magic, appeared to him as though they moved fast.
66.arberry: 'No,' said Moses. 'Do you cast!' And lo, it seemed to him, by their sorcery, their ropes and their staffs were sliding;

67.sahih_international: And he sensed within himself apprehension, did Moses.
67.pickthall: And Moses conceived a fear in his mind.
67.yusuf_ali: So Moses conceived in his mind a (sort of) fear.
67.shakir: So Musa conceived in his mind a fear.
67.mohsin_khan: So Musa (Moses) conceived a fear in himself.
67.arberry: and Moses conceived a fear within him.

68.sahih_international: Allah said, "Fear not. Indeed, it is you who are superior.
68.pickthall: We said: Fear not! Lo! thou art the higher.
68.yusuf_ali: We said: "Fear not! for thou hast indeed the upper hand:
68.shakir: We said: Fear not, surely you shall be the uppermost,
68.muhammad_sarwar: We told him, "Do not be afraid for you will be the winner.
68.mohsin_khan: We (Allah) said: "Fear not! Surely, you will have the upper hand.
68.arberry: We said unto him, 'Fear not; surely thou art the uppermost.

69.sahih_international: And throw what is in your right hand; it will swallow up what they have crafted. What they have crafted is but the trick of a magician, and the magician will not succeed wherever he is."
69.pickthall: Throw that which is in thy right hand! It will eat up that which they have made. Lo! that which they have made is but a wizard's artifice, and a wizard shall not be successful to whatever point (of skill) he may attain.
69.yusuf_ali: "Throw that which is in thy right hand: Quickly will it swallow up that which they have faked what they have faked is but a magician's trick: and the magician thrives not, (no matter) where he goes."
69.shakir: And cast down what is in your right hand; it shall devour what they have wrought; they have wrought only the plan of a magician, and the magician shall not be successful wheresoever he may come from.
69.muhammad_sarwar: Throw down what is in your right hand and it will swallow up all that they have performed; theirs is only a magical performance. Magicians can find no happiness in whatever they do."
69.mohsin_khan: "And throw that which is in your right hand! It will swallow up that which they have made. That which they have made is only a magician's trick, and the magician will never be successful, no matter whatever amount (of skill) he may attain."
69.arberry: Cast down what is in thy right hand, and it shall swallow what they have fashioned; for they have fashioned only the guile of a sorcerer, and the sorcerer prospers not; wherever he goes.'

70.sahih_international: So the magicians fell down in prostration. They said, "We have believed in the Lord of Aaron and Moses."
70.pickthall: Then the wizards were (all) flung down prostrate, crying: We believe in the Lord of Aaron and Moses.
70.yusuf_ali: So the magicians were thrown down to prostration: they said, "We believe in the Lord of Aaron and Moses".
70.shakir: And the magicians were cast down making obeisance; they said: We believe in the Lord of Haroun and Musa.
70.muhammad_sarwar: The magicians bowed down in prostration saying, "We believe in the Lord of Moses and Aaron".
70.mohsin_khan: So the magicians fell down prostrate. They said: "We believe in the Lord of Harun (Aaron) and Musa (Moses)."
70.arberry: And the sorcerers cast themselves down prostrating. 'We believe,' they said, 'in the Lord of Aaron and Moses.'

71.sahih_international: [Pharaoh] said, "You believed him before I gave you permission. Indeed, he is your leader who has taught you magic. So I will surely cut off your hands and your feet on opposite sides, and I will crucify you on the trunks of palm trees, and you will surely know which of us is more severe in [giving] punishment and more enduring."
71.pickthall: (Pharaoh) said: Ye put faith in him before I give you leave. Lo! he is your chief who taught you magic. Now surely I shall cut off your hands and your feet alternately, and I shall crucify you on the trunks of palm trees, and ye shall know for certain which of us hath sterner and more lasting punishment.
71.yusuf_ali: (Pharaoh) said: "Believe ye in Him before I give you permission? Surely this must be your leader, who has taught you magic! be sure I will cut off your hands and feet on opposite sides, and I will have you crucified on trunks of palm-trees: so shall ye know for certain, which of us can give the more severe and the more lasting punishment!"
71.shakir: (Firon) said: You believe in him before I give you leave; most surely he is the chief of you who taught you enchantment, therefore I will certainly cut off your hands and your feet on opposite sides, and I will certainly crucify you on the trunks of the palm trees, and certainly you will come to know which of us is the more severe and the more abiding in chastising.
71.muhammad_sarwar: The Pharaoh said, "Since you believed in him without my permission, then Moses certainly must be your chief who has taught you magic. I shall cut your hands and feet on alternate sides and crucify you on the trunk of the palm-tree. You shall certainly find which among us can afflict a more severe and lasting punishment".
71.mohsin_khan: [Fir'aun (Pharaoh)] said: "Believe you in him [Musa (Moses)] before I give you permission? Verily! He is your chief who taught you magic. So I will surely cut off your hands and feet on opposite sides, and I will surely crucify you on the trunks of date-palms, and you shall surely know which of us [I (Fir'aun - Pharaoh) or the Lord of Musa (Moses) (Allah)] can give the severe and more lasting torment."
71.arberry: Pharaoh said, 'Have you believed him before I gave you leave? Why, he is the chief of you, the same that taught you sorcery; I shall assuredly cut off alternately your hands and feet, then I shall crucify you upon the trunks of palm-trees; you shall know of a certainty which of us is more terrible in chastisement, and more abiding.'

72.sahih_international: They said, "Never will we prefer you over what has come to us of clear proofs and [over] He who created us. So decree whatever you are to decree. You can only decree for this worldly life.
72.pickthall: They said: We choose thee not above the clear proofs that have come unto us, and above Him Who created us. So decree what thou wilt decree. Thou wilt end for us only this life of the world.
72.yusuf_ali: They said: "Never shall we regard thee as more than the Clear Signs that have come to us, or than Him Who created us! so decree whatever thou desirest to decree: for thou canst only decree (touching) the life of this world.
72.shakir: They said: We do not prefer you to what has come to us of clear arguments and to He Who made us, therefore decide what you are going to decide; you can only decide about this world's life.
72.muhammad_sarwar: They (the magicians) said, "We would never prefer you to the miracles that we have seen or to our Creator. Do what you want. This life is only for a short time.
72.mohsin_khan: They said: "We prefer you not over the clear signs that have come to us, and to Him (Allah) Who created us. So decree whatever you desire to decree, for you can only decree (regarding) this life of the world.
72.arberry: They said, 'We will not prefer thee over the clear signs that have come to us, nor over Him who originated us. Decide then what thou wilt decide; thou canst only decide touching this present life.

73.sahih_international: Indeed, we have believed in our Lord that He may forgive us our sins and what you compelled us [to do] of magic. And Allah is better and more enduring."
73.pickthall: Lo! we believe in our Lord, that He may forgive us our sins and the magic unto which thou didst force us. Allah is better and more lasting.
73.yusuf_ali: "For us, we have believed in our Lord: may He forgive us our faults, and the magic to which thou didst compel us: for Allah is Best and Most Abiding."
73.shakir: Surely we believe in our Lord that He may forgive us our sins and the magic to which you compelled us; and Allah is better and more abiding.
73.muhammad_sarwar: We have faith in our Lord so that He will forgive our sins and our magical performances that you forced us to show. God is better than all things and His rewards last longer."
73.mohsin_khan: "Verily! We have believed in our Lord, that He may forgive us our faults, and the magic to which you did compel us. And Allah is better as regards reward in comparison to your [Fir'aun's (Pharaoh)] reward, and more lasting (as regards punishment in comparison to your punishment)."
73.arberry: We believe in our Lord, that He may pardon us our offences, and the sorcery thou hast constrained us to practise; God is better, and more abiding.'

74.sahih_international: Indeed, whoever comes to his Lord as a criminal - indeed, for him is Hell; he will neither die therein nor live.
74.pickthall: Lo! whoso cometh guilty unto his Lord, verily for him is hell. There he will neither die nor live.
74.yusuf_ali: Verily he who comes to his Lord as a sinner (at Judgment),- for him is Hell: therein shall he neither die nor live.
74.shakir: Whoever comes to his Lord (being) guilty, for him is surely hell; he shall not die therein, nor shall he live.
74.muhammad_sarwar: The dwelling place of one who comes into the presence of his Lord as a criminal will be hell wherein he will never die nor enjoy his life.
74.mohsin_khan: Verily! Whoever comes to his Lord as a Mujrim (criminal, polytheist, disbeliever in the Oneness of Allah and His Messengers, sinner, etc.), then surely, for him is Hell, therein he will neither die nor live.
74.arberry: Whosoever comes unto his Lord a sinner, for him awaits Gehenna wherein he shall neither die nor live.

75.sahih_international: But whoever comes to Him as a believer having done righteous deeds - for those will be the highest degrees [in position]:
75.pickthall: But whoso cometh unto Him a believer, having done good works, for such are the high stations;
75.yusuf_ali: But such as come to Him as Believers who have worked righteous deeds,- for them are ranks exalted,-
75.shakir: And whoever comes to Him a believer (and) he has done good deeds indeed, these it is who shall have the high ranks,
75.muhammad_sarwar: One who comes into the presence of his Lord with faith and righteous deeds
75.mohsin_khan: But whoever comes to Him (Allah) as a believer (in the Oneness of Allah, etc.), and has done righteous good deeds, for such are the high ranks (in the Hereafter),
75.arberry: And whoso comes unto Him a believer having done deeds of righteousness, those -- for them await the most sublime degrees;

76.sahih_international: Gardens of perpetual residence beneath which rivers flow, wherein they abide eternally. And that is the reward of one who purifies himself.
76.pickthall: Gardens of Eden underneath which rivers flow, wherein they will abide for ever. That is the reward of him who groweth.
76.yusuf_ali: Gardens of Eternity, beneath which flow rivers: they will dwell therein for aye: such is the reward of those who purify themselves (from evil).
76.shakir: The gardens of perpetuity, beneath which rivers flow, to abide therein; and this is the reward of him who has purified himself.
76.muhammad_sarwar: will be rewarded by high status in the gardens of Eden wherein streams flow. Such will be the reward of those who purify themselves.
76.mohsin_khan: 'Adn (Edn) Paradise (everlasting Gardens), under which rivers flow, wherein they will abide forever: such is the reward of those who purify themselves [(by abstaining from all kinds of sins and evil deeds) which Allah has forbidden and by doing all that which Allah has ordained)].
76.arberry: Gardens of Eden, underneath which rivers flow, therein dwelling forever; that is the recompense of the self-purified.

77.sahih_international: And We had inspired to Moses, "Travel by night with My servants and strike for them a dry path through the sea; you will not fear being overtaken [by Pharaoh] nor be afraid [of drowning]."
77.pickthall: And verily We inspired Moses, saying: Take away My slaves by night and strike for them a dry path in the sea, fearing not to be overtaken, neither being afraid (of the sea).
77.yusuf_ali: We sent an inspiration to Moses: "Travel by night with My servants, and strike a dry path for them through the sea, without fear of being overtaken (by Pharaoh) and without (any other) fear."
77.shakir: And certainly We revealed to Musa, saying: Travel by night with My servants, then make for them a dry path in the sea, not fearing to be overtaken, nor being afraid.
77.muhammad_sarwar: We sent revelations to Moses telling him, "Travel with My servants during the night and strike a dry road across the sea (for them). Have no fear of being overtaken (by the Pharaoh) nor of anything else".
77.mohsin_khan: And indeed We inspired Musa (Moses) (saying): "Travel by night with Ibadi (My slaves) and strike a dry path for them in the sea, fearing neither to be overtaken [by Fir'aun (Pharaoh)] nor being afraid (of drowning in the sea)."
77.arberry: Also We revealed unto Moses, 'Go with My servants by night; strike for them a dry path in the sea, fearing not overtaking, neither afraid.'

78.sahih_international: So Pharaoh pursued them with his soldiers, and there covered them from the sea that which covered them,
78.pickthall: Then Pharaoh followed them with his hosts and there covered them that which did cover them of the sea.
78.yusuf_ali: Then Pharaoh pursued them with his forces, but the waters completely overwhelmed them and covered them up.
78.shakir: And Firon followed them with his armies, so there came upon them of the sea that which came upon them.
78.muhammad_sarwar: The Pharaoh and his army chased Moses and his people but were drowned by the sea.
78.mohsin_khan: Then Fir'aun (Pharaoh) pursued them with his hosts, but the sea-water completely overwhelmed them and covered them up.
78.arberry: Pharaoh followed them with his hosts, but they were overwhelmed by the sea;

79.sahih_international: And Pharaoh led his people astray and did not guide [them].
79.pickthall: And Pharaoh led his folk astray, he did not guide them.
79.yusuf_ali: Pharaoh led his people astray instead of leading them aright.
79.shakir: And Firon led astray his people and he did not guide (them) aright.
79.muhammad_sarwar: The Pharaoh and his people had gone away from guidance.
79.mohsin_khan: And Fir'aun (Pharaoh) led his people astray, and he did not guide them.
79.arberry: so Pharaoh had led his people astray, and was no guide to them.

80.sahih_international: O Children of Israel, We delivered you from your enemy, and We made an appointment with you at the right side of the mount, and We sent down to you manna and quails,
80.pickthall: O Children of Israel! We delivered you from your enemy, and we made a covenant with you on the holy mountain's side, and sent down on you the manna and the quails,
80.yusuf_ali: O ye Children of Israel! We delivered you from your enemy, and We made a Covenant with you on the right side of Mount (Sinai), and We sent down to you Manna and quails:
80.shakir: O children of Israel! indeed We delivered you from your enemy, and We made a covenant with you on the blessed side of the mountain, and We sent to you the manna and the quails.
80.muhammad_sarwar: Children of Israel, We saved you from your enemy and promised to settle you on the right side of the peaceful Mount Tur (Sinai)
80.mohsin_khan: O Children of Israel! We delivered you from your enemy, and We made a covenant with you on the right side of the Mount, and We sent down to you Al-Manna and quails,
80.arberry: Children of Israel, We delivered you from your enemy; and We made covenant with you upon the right side of the Mount, and sent down on you manna and quails:

81.sahih_international: [Saying], "Eat from the good things with which We have provided you and do not transgress [or oppress others] therein, lest My anger should descend upon you. And he upon whom My anger descends has certainly fallen."
81.pickthall: (Saying): Eat of the good things wherewith We have provided you, and transgress not in respect thereof lest My wrath come upon you: and he on whom My wrath cometh, he is lost indeed.
81.yusuf_ali: (Saying): "Eat of the good things We have provided for your sustenance, but commit no excess therein, lest My Wrath should justly descend on you: and those on whom descends My Wrath do perish indeed!
81.shakir: Eat of the good things We have given you for sustenance, and be not inordinate with respect to them, lest My wrath should be due to you, and to whomsoever My wrath is due be shall perish indeed.
81.muhammad_sarwar: and We sent you manna and quails.
81.mohsin_khan: (Saying) eat of the Taiyibat (good lawful things) wherewith We have provided you, and commit no oppression therein, lest My Anger should justly descend on you. And he on whom My Anger descends, he is indeed perished.
81.arberry: 'Eat of the good things wherewith We have provided you; but exceed not therein, or My anger shall alight on you; and on whomsoever My anger alights, that man is hurled to ruin.

82.sahih_international: But indeed, I am the Perpetual Forgiver of whoever repents and believes and does righteousness and then continues in guidance.
82.pickthall: And lo! verily I am Forgiving toward him who repenteth and believeth and doeth good, and afterward walketh aright.
82.yusuf_ali: "But, without doubt, I am (also) He that forgives again and again, to those who repent, believe, and do right, who,- in fine, are ready to receive true guidance."
82.shakir: And most surely I am most Forgiving to him who repents and believes and does good, then continues to follow the right direction.
82.muhammad_sarwar: I allowed you to consume the pure sustenance which We had given you but not to become rebels, lest you become subject to My wrath. Whoever becomes subject to My wrath will certainly be destroyed. I am All-forgiving to the righteously striving believers who repent and follow the right guidance.
82.mohsin_khan: And verily, I am indeed Forgiving to him who repents, believes (in My Oneness, and associates none in worship with Me) and does righteous good deeds, and then remains constant in doing them, (till his death).
82.arberry: Yet I am All-forgiving to him who repents and believes, and does righteousness, and at last is guided.'

83.sahih_international: [Allah] said, "And what made you hasten from your people, O Moses?"
83.pickthall: And (it was said): What hath made thee hasten from thy folk, O Moses?
83.yusuf_ali: (When Moses was up on the Mount, Allah said:) "What made thee hasten in advance of thy people, O Moses?"
83.shakir: And what caused you to hasten from your people, O Musa?
83.muhammad_sarwar: The Lord asked, "Moses, what made you attend your appointment with Me before your people?"
83.mohsin_khan: "And what made you hasten from your people, O Musa (Moses)?"
83.arberry: 'What has sped thee far from thy people, Moses?'

84.sahih_international: He said, "They are close upon my tracks, and I hastened to You, my Lord, that You be pleased."
84.pickthall: He said: They are close upon my track. I hastened unto Thee, my Lord, that Thou mightest be well pleased.
84.yusuf_ali: He replied: "Behold, they are close on my footsteps: I hastened to thee, O my Lord, to please thee."
84.shakir: He said: They are here on my track and I hastened on to Thee, my Lord, that Thou mightest be pleased.
84.muhammad_sarwar: Moses replied, "They are just behind me. I came earlier to seek Your pleasure".
84.mohsin_khan: He said: "They are close on my footsteps, and I hastened to You, O my Lord, that You might be pleased."
84.arberry: 'They are upon my tracks,' Moses said. 'I have hastened, Lord, only that I may please Thee.'

85.sahih_international: [Allah] said, "But indeed, We have tried your people after you [departed], and the Samiri has led them astray."
85.pickthall: He said: Lo! We have tried thy folk in thine absence, and As-Samiri hath misled them.
85.yusuf_ali: (Allah) said: "We have tested thy people in thy absence: the Samiri has led them astray."
85.shakir: He said: So surely We have tried your people after you, and the Samiri has led them astray.
85.muhammad_sarwar: The Lord said, "We tested your people after you left them and the Samiri made them go astray."
85.mohsin_khan: (Allah) said: "Verily! We have tried your people in your absence, and As-Samiri has led them astray."
85.arberry: Said He, 'We have tempted thy people since thou didst leave them. The Samaritan has misled them into error.'

86.sahih_international: So Moses returned to his people, angry and grieved. He said, "O my people, did your Lord not make you a good promise? Then, was the time [of its fulfillment] too long for you, or did you wish that wrath from your Lord descend upon you, so you broke your promise [of obedience] to me?"
86.pickthall: Then Moses went back unto his folk, angry and sad. He said: O my people! Hath not your Lord promised you a fair promise? Did the time appointed then appear too long for you, or did ye wish that wrath from your Lord should come upon you, that ye broke tryst with me?
86.yusuf_ali: So Moses returned to his people in a state of indignation and sorrow. He said: "O my people! did not your Lord make a handsome promise to you? Did then the promise seem to you long (in coming)? Or did ye desire that Wrath should descend from your Lord on you, and so ye broke your promise to me?"
86.shakir: So Musa returned to his people wrathful, sorrowing. Said he: O my people! did not your Lord promise you a goodly promise: did then the time seem long to you, or did you wish that displeasure from your Lord should be due to you, so that you broke (your) promise to me?
86.muhammad_sarwar: Moses, sad and angry, returned to his people saying, "My people, did not the Lord make you a gracious promise? Why did you disregard your appointment with me? Was it because of the long time or did you want to become subject to the wrath of your Lord?"
86.mohsin_khan: Then Musa (Moses) returned to his people in a state of anger and sorrow. He said: "O my people! Did not your Lord promise you a fair promise? Did then the promise seem to you long in coming? Or did you desire that wrath should descend from your Lord on you, so you broke your promise to me (i.e. disbelieving in Allah and worshipping the calf)?"
86.arberry: Then Moses returned very angry and sorrowful to his people, saying, 'My people, did your Lord not promise a fair promise to you? Did the time of the covenant seem so long to you, or did you desire that anger should alight on you from your Lord, so that you failed in your tryst with me?'

87.sahih_international: They said, "We did not break our promise to you by our will, but we were made to carry burdens from the ornaments of the people [of Pharaoh], so we threw them [into the fire], and thus did the Samiri throw."
87.pickthall: They said: We broke not tryst with thee of our own will, but we were laden with burdens of ornaments of the folk, then cast them (in the fire), for thus As-Samiri proposed.
87.yusuf_ali: They said: "We broke not the promise to thee, as far as lay in our power: but we were made to carry the weight of the ornaments of the (whole) people, and we threw them (into the fire), and that was what the Samiri suggested.
87.shakir: They said: We did not break (our) promise to you of our own accord, but we were made to bear the burdens of the ornaments of the people, then we made a casting of them, and thus did the Samiri suggest.
87.muhammad_sarwar: They replied, "We did not go against our promise with you out of our own accord. We were forced to carry people's ornaments. We threw them away and so did the Samiri.
87.mohsin_khan: They said: "We broke not the promise to you, of our own will, but we were made to carry the weight of the ornaments of the [Fir'aun's (Pharaoh)] people, then we cast them (into the fire), and that was what As-Samiri suggested."
87.arberry: 'We have not failed in our tryst with thee,' they said, 'of our volition; but we were loaded with fardels, even the ornaments of the people, and we cast them, as the Samaritan also threw them, into the fire.'

88.sahih_international: And he extracted for them [the statue of] a calf which had a lowing sound, and they said, "This is your god and the god of Moses, but he forgot."
88.pickthall: Then he produced for them a calf, of saffron hue, which gave forth a lowing sound. And they cried: This is your god and the god of Moses, but he hath forgotten.
88.yusuf_ali: "Then he brought out (of the fire) before the (people) the image of a calf: It seemed to low: so they said: This is your god, and the god of Moses, but (Moses) has forgotten!"
88.shakir: So he brought forth for them a calf, a (mere) body, which had a mooing sound, so they said: This is your god and the god of Musa, but he forgot.
88.muhammad_sarwar: Then the Samiri forged the body of a motionless calf which gave out a hollow sound." The people said, "This is your Lord and the Lord of Moses whom he (Moses) forgot to mention".
88.mohsin_khan: Then he took out (of the fire) for them a statue of a calf which seemed to low. They said: "This is your ilah (god), and the ilah (god) of Musa (Moses), but [Musa (Moses)] has forgotten (his god).'"
88.arberry: (Then he brought out for them a Calf, a mere body that lowed; and they said, 'This is your god, and the god of Moses, whom he has forgotten.'

89.sahih_international: Did they not see that it could not return to them any speech and that it did not possess for them any harm or benefit?
89.pickthall: See they not, then, that it returneth no saying unto them and possesseth for them neither hurt nor use?
89.yusuf_ali: Could they not see that it could not return them a word (for answer), and that it had no power either to harm them or to do them good?
89.shakir: What! could they not see that it did not return to them a reply, and (that) it did not control any harm or benefit for them?
89.muhammad_sarwar: Did they not consider that the calf could not give them any answer, nor it could harm or benefit them?
89.mohsin_khan: Did they not see that it could not return them a word (for answer), and that it had no power either to harm them or to do them good?
89.arberry: What? Did they not see that thing returned no speech unto them, neither had any power to hurt or profit them?

90.sahih_international: And Aaron had already told them before [the return of Moses], "O my people, you are only being tested by it, and indeed, your Lord is the Most Merciful, so follow me and obey my order."
90.pickthall: And Aaron indeed had told them beforehand: O my people! Ye are but being seduced therewith, for lo! your Lord is the Beneficent, so follow me and obey my order.
90.yusuf_ali: Aaron had already, before this said to them: "O my people! ye are being tested in this: for verily your Lord is (Allah) Most Gracious; so follow me and obey my command."
90.shakir: And certainly Haroun had said to them before: O my people! you are only tried by it, and surely your Lord is the Beneficent Allah, therefore follow me and obey my order.
90.muhammad_sarwar: Aaron had told them before, "My people, you are deceived by the calf. Your Lord is the Beneficent God. Follow me and obey my orders".
90.mohsin_khan: And Harun (Aaron) indeed had said to them beforehand: "O my people! You are being tried in this, and verily, your Lord is (Allah) the Most Beneficent, so follow me and obey my order."
90.arberry: Yet Aaron had aforetime said to them, 'My people, you have been tempted by this thing, no more; surety your Lord is the All-merciful; therefore follow me, and obey my commandment!'

91.sahih_international: They said, "We will never cease being devoted to the calf until Moses returns to us."
91.pickthall: They said: We shall by no means cease to be its votaries till Moses return unto us.
91.yusuf_ali: They had said: "We will not abandon this cult, but we will devote ourselves to it until Moses returns to us."
91.shakir: They said: We will by no means cease to keep to its worship until Musa returns to us.
91.muhammad_sarwar: They said, "We shall continue worshipping the calf until Moses comes back."
91.mohsin_khan: They said: "We will not stop worshipping it (i.e. the calf), until Musa (Moses) returns to us."
91.arberry: 'We will not cease,' they said, 'to cleave to it, until Moses returns to us.')

92.sahih_international: [Moses] said, "O Aaron, what prevented you, when you saw them going astray,
92.pickthall: He (Moses) said: O Aaron! What held thee back when thou didst see them gone astray,
92.yusuf_ali: (Moses) said: "O Aaron! what kept thee back, when thou sawest them going wrong,
92.shakir: (Musa) said: O Haroun! what prevented you, when you saw them going astray,
92.muhammad_sarwar: Then Moses asked Aaron, "What made you not follow me when you saw them in error?
92.mohsin_khan: [Musa (Moses)] said: "O Harun (Aaron)! What stopped you when you saw them going astray;
92.arberry: Moses said, 'What prevented thee, Aaron, when thou sawest them in error,

93.sahih_international: From following me? Then have you disobeyed my order?"
93.pickthall: That thou followedst me not? Hast thou then disobeyed my order?
93.yusuf_ali: "From following me? Didst thou then disobey my order?"
93.shakir: So that you did not follow me? Did you then disobey my order?
93.mohsin_khan: "That you followed me not (according to my advice to you)? Have you then disobeyed my order?"
93.arberry: so that thou didst not follow after me? Didst thou then disobey my commandment?'

94.sahih_international: [Aaron] said, "O son of my mother, do not seize [me] by my beard or by my head. Indeed, I feared that you would say, 'You caused division among the Children of Israel, and you did not observe [or await] my word.' "
94.pickthall: He said: O son of my mother! Clutch not my beard nor my head! I feared lest thou shouldst say: Thou hast caused division among the Children of Israel, and hast not waited for my word.
94.yusuf_ali: (Aaron) replied: "O son of my mother! Seize (me) not by my beard nor by (the hair of) my head! Truly I feared lest thou shouldst say, 'Thou has caused a division among the children of Israel, and thou didst not respect my word!'"
94.shakir: He said: O son of my mother! seize me not by my beard nor by my head; surely I was afraid lest you should say: You have caused a division among the children of Israel and not waited for my word.
94.muhammad_sarwar: Aaron replied, "Son of my mother, do not seize me by my beard or head. I was afraid that you might consider me responsible for causing discord among the children of Israel and would not pay attention to my words."
94.mohsin_khan: He [Harun (Aaron)] said: "O son of my mother! Seize (me) not by my beard, nor by my head! Verily, I feared lest you should say: 'You have caused a division among the Children of Israel, and you have not respected my word!' "
94.arberry: 'Son of my mother,' Aaron said, 'take me not by the beard, or the head! I was fearful that thou wouldst say, "Thou hast divided the Children of Israel, and thou hast not observed my word."

95.sahih_international: [Moses] said, "And what is your case, O Samiri?"
95.pickthall: (Moses) said: And what hast thou to say, O Samiri?
95.yusuf_ali: (Moses) said: "What then is thy case, O Samiri?"
95.shakir: He said: What was then your object, O Samiri?
95.muhammad_sarwar: Moses asked, "Samiri, what were your motives?"
95.mohsin_khan: [Musa (Moses)] said: "And what is the matter with you. O Samiri? (i.e. why did you do so?)"
95.arberry: Moses said, 'And thou, Samaritan, what was thy business?'

96.sahih_international: He said, "I saw what they did not see, so I took a handful [of dust] from the track of the messenger and threw it, and thus did my soul entice me."
96.pickthall: He said: I perceived what they perceive not, so I seized a handful from the footsteps of the messenger, and then threw it in. Thus my soul commended to me.
96.yusuf_ali: He replied: "I saw what they saw not: so I took a handful (of dust) from the footprint of the Messenger, and threw it (into the calf): thus did my soul suggest to me."
96.shakir: He said: I saw (Jibreel) what they did not see, so I took a handful (of the dust) from the footsteps of the messenger, then I threw it in the casting; thus did my soul commend to me
96.muhammad_sarwar: He replied, "I had the skill (of carving) which they did not have. I followed some of the Messengers's (Moses) tradition, but I then ignored it. Thus, my soul prompted me (to carve a golden calf with an artificial hollow sound).
96.mohsin_khan: (Samiri) said: "I saw what they saw not, so I took a handful (of dust) from the hoof print of the messenger [Jibrael's (Gabriel) horse] and threw it [into the fire in which were put the ornaments of the Fir'aun's (Pharaoh) people, or into the calf]. Thus my inner-self suggested to me."
